chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Basir said to him, 'The people of Mecca reproached you for not kissing the Black Stone, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did kiss it.' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he reached the Stone, they would make way for him, but they do not make way for me.'

key_terms.يُفْرِجُوا لَهُ: They would make way for him

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq not kiss the Black Stone during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that his omission of kissing the Black Stone was a contextual necessity rather than a rejection of the Sunnah, as the dense crowds prevented him from receiving the same honor shown to the Prophet. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly principle that ritual acts are often performed with full awareness of their social and physical conditions, distinguishing between the ideal practice and its practical execution in a busy environment. It also highlights the unique reverence accorded to the Prophet during his lifetime, which serves as a benchmark for understanding the Imam's own status and actions.
